deals.evidence: Under the terms of the 20-year agreement, the City of Everett will receive an estimated $91.7 million in total community value
deals.headline: Kraft Group and City of Everett reach community agreement for Revolution stadium
deals.summary: 20-year community impact agreement for a privately funded ~25,000-seat Revolution stadium on the former Mystic Generating Station site in Everett, MA: an estimated $91.7m in community value to the city, separate from an estimated $100m Kraft Group commitment to environmental cleanup, plus $2.25 per ticket sold.

chief_executive.evidence: As President of the New England Revolution, Brian Bilello reports directly to the Kraft family and oversees all aspects of the club’s business and soccer operations.
chief_executive.name: Brian Bilello
chief_executive.title: President

honours.evidence: In 2021, Kraft saw the Revolution set an MLS record with 73 regular season points en route to the club’s first Supporters’ Shield title.

operating_result.evidence: The estimates of teams’ revenue and operating income (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization) reflect the 2025 season
operating_result.source_name: Forbes (estimate), The Most Valuable MLS Teams 2026

stadium_owner.detail: Gillette Stadium is held by the Kraft family (Kraft Group), the club's owner, not by the club itself; it is shared with the NFL's New England Patriots. A club-specific, privately funded ~25,000-seat stadium is planned in Everett, MA.
stadium_owner.evidence: His holdings include the New England Revolution, New England Patriots, Gillette Stadium

founded_evidence: On June 6, 1995, the Kraft family became the founding Investor/Operator of the Revolution, joining Major League Soccer (MLS) as one of its 10 charter clubs for its inaugural season in 1996.
name: New England Revolution
notes: Founded: the Kraft family became Investor/Operator on 6 June 1995; first season 1996. Stadium capacity is Gillette Stadium's full (NFL) capacity; the Revolution play to a reduced soccer configuration no citable page stated. Forbes figures are estimates for the 2025 season; Forbes is paywalled/403 so the Internet Archive snapshot of the Forbes article is cited (original: https://www.forbes.com/sites/justinbirnbaum/2026/02/13/the-most-valuable-mls-teams-2026/). Forbes lists Key Owner: Kraft family. No stake percentage, legal entity, socials, attendance or shirt sponsor found on a citable page; MLS is a single-entity league, so there are no club accounts. Everett stadium: privately funded per the club's FAQ, regulatory approvals pending (MEPA process 2026).

owners.evidence: The Kraft family was one of the original founders of Major League Soccer (MLS) in 1996 and founded the New England Revolution as one of the league’s 10 charter clubs.
owners.name: Kraft family (The Kraft Group)

ownership_summary: Owned by the Kraft family through the Kraft Group (Robert K. Kraft and Jonathan A. Kraft are the club's Investor/Operators), who founded the club as an MLS charter member in 1995. No institutional or minority investor is disclosed.
